name: Blackfriars Council condemns Wycliffe
summary: An English synod at Blackfriars in London condemns twenty-four propositions drawn from the writings of John Wycliffe, including his rejection of transubstantiation and the temporal endowment of the Church. Wycliffe retires to Lutterworth, where he completes the translation of the Vulgate into Middle English.

_quarry.structural_significance: First major proto-Reformation condemnation in England; Wycliffe's vernacular Bible and 'Lollard' followers anticipate Hussite and later Reformation themes by a century.
